open_questions: Why transit 20 is shallow (1306 ppm) and transit 21 deep (29666 ppm) on a 14.8 d period; ground-based transit check needed.
RUWE 1.039 and modest duration excess (observed 2.998 h vs central 1.936 h, ratio 1.55) are unexplained but do not favour a binary alone.
UV contamination from close star at 34.7 arcsec (delta_mag 0.15) mentioned in similar cases
dossier.public_summary: Four dips on a small cool star suggest a ~3.7 Earth-radius object on a 14.8-day orbit with a flat, central shape and no secondary eclipse. A strong odd-even difference looks like a binary but is caused by one shallow and one deep transit that do not follow a steady pattern; the depth is steady between sectors. The dip does not localize to a neighbour star, favouring a planet with a few bad individual transits to explain.

reasons.why: Large odd-even difference is a strong binary signature, but transit_depths shows it is driven by two outliers not a regular alternation.
Depth is not consistent across the four individual transits, with one very shallow (-5 sigma) and one very deep (+4.6 sigma), so the odd/even pattern does not persist transit-to-transit.
Shape is flat-bottomed and central (fit_b 1.737e-7, fit_k 0.1182), favouring a planet over a grazing EB, and duration.ratio 1.549 is only mildly long.
No real change in depth between sectors or within TESS-SPOC, and centroid has no off-target suspect within 1 px (plausible_within_1px 0).

Undiluted depth implies a 3.7 Earth-radius planet, below the stellar limit, with no secondary (secondary snr 2.4) and no phase-curve signature (phase_curve amplitude 1547 ppm, ratio_to_depth 0.1022, chi2 12.92/9).
